source.title: A Differential Game Theoretic Neural Optimizer for Training Residual Networks
source.authors: Guan-Horng Liu; T. Chen; Evangelos A. Theodorou

record.file_problem: Full paper text provided, including supplementary material.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports classification training losses for residual networks under several optimizers and datasets, including CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. It tests whether the tested training recipes achieve low training loss, using different optimizers and architectures from the versions’ specific recipe comparisons.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports train loss for each dataset and optimizer, including GT-DDP variants; Fig. 6a gives CIFAR-10 training curves. The paper does not report training classification error, corrupted or random labels, smaller-model or early-stopping comparisons, or the initialization, depth-without-shortcuts, batch-normalization, and stability-limit comparisons named in the versions. Cited prior results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses residual networks to evaluate its proposed optimizer. It reports training loss, validation accuracy and variation across seeds, but no training classification-error rates or comparisons testing V2–V6. Its optimizer-performance comparisons do not test any supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: GT-DDP extends DDP to residual and convolutional architectures and improves convergence and robustness in their classification experiments, with generally better or comparable validation accuracy. These are aggregate conclusions; Table 2 includes slight degradations in some comparisons.
record.recipe_differences: Tests GT-DDP as a new optimizer integrated with SGD, RMSprop, Adam and EKFAC on residual-network classification tasks; not the versions’ specific comparison recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and optimizer change whether GT-DDP lowers the reported train loss relative to its baseline; the paper also reports training-variation results across random seeds and learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: GT-DDP variants usually lower reported training loss relative to their corresponding optimizers; several comparisons are equal at displayed precision or slightly worse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture-aware GT-DDP updates can improve training-loss convergence relative to matched optimizer baselines on the tested residual networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 6b and 8 report reduced performance variation across random seeds, including comparisons at three learning rates per optimizer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GT-DDP feedback updates can reduce variation across random initializations under the tested hyperparameters.

record.code_released: https://github.com/Thrandis/EKFAC-pytorch (stated as the EKFAC baseline implementation; no GT-DDP repository stated)
record.problems: The main table aggregates over 6 random seeds but gives no uncertainty values for the training-loss comparisons. Training loss is reported rather than classification error, and the paper does not test corrupted/random labels or the other version-specific conditions.
record.rows_left_out: None. Table 2 training-loss results are retained for all five datasets and eight GT-DDP variants.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error under SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels, and the stated size, stopping and regularization conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU local-minimum frequency and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Effects of activation-matched initialization, signal propagation and orthogonality on training speed and trainable depth.
Recovery or divergence relative to the initial stability threshold, curvature reduction and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including the Fixup alternative.

record.verdict_notes: The reported training-loss values match Table 2. All subjects are optimizer variants rather than models. The original row states incorrectly describe relative optimizer improvements as effects of V1; unavailable classification-error measurements warrant cannot_determine, not partial, absent or reversed. The record's rows_left_out also incorrectly refers to eight GT-DDP variants: Table 2 contains four baselines and four GT-DDP variants.

versions.untested_parts: Training loss is reported, but the claim’s classification-error measure, corrupted or random labels, SGD/Adam-only formulation from random initialization, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes are not tested as described.

reader_labels.condition: GT-DDP training-loss comparisons across the five datasets
reader_labels.reason: Most integrated optimizers show lower reported training loss than their baselines, but several comparisons are equal or worse (R5, R10, R16, R17, R20); training loss does not directly establish near-zero classification error (R1–R20).
